chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: Lil's role in Louis Armstrong's career
summary: DeMichael and Saunders agree Lil got Louis away from Oliver, taught him to read, ran business and set up the Hot Five.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, I always felt that she was the reason for Louis' success, in urging him to leave Oliver and go with Henderson.
Right, right.
And then lining up all this work for him, getting back here and I would imagine that she had line up the OK recording contract for the Hot Five before --
Right, well, she was a great business-woman because, see, she had her band in the Dreamland Cafe, and then she and -- because, see, at that time, he was working
with Erskine Tate, too, at the Vendome.
Right.

And so she had him to come over -- after he would finish there he would come over and work with her. And then this is how the association -- and finally they got married. Started going together -- but that was her band. He was working in her band then.
Yeah.
And then later on, in later years, he got the Hot Five, and then she --
Well, the Hot Five, the first records were made soon after he came back to Chicago to work --
Fletcher.
After he left Fletcher and came to work with Lil at the Dreamland.
Right, right.
Then within a month they made the first Hot Five record.
Right, right.
Richard M. Jones was (inaudible).
Yeah, right, right.
But I've always thought that Lil must have lined that all up.
Lil was so instrumental in Louis' success, more so that people would really realize. Because

she'd talk -- he was just a happy-go-lucky horn blower, like a lot of the musicians, no business ability or nothing. And so she put it down to him like it was and everything, but she got him away from Joe Oliver.
That's what Earl Hines -- Earl Hines told me, the day that Louis died, -- I interviewed him when he was in town --
Yeah.
And he said he and Louis were a couple of young Turks, they'd get through at the Sunset, and Louis always kept his mouthpiece in his pocket.
Right, right.
And they'd go out and sit in, --
Right, right, right.
-- and play until dawn.

Right, right, right, right. And then, like I told you about the baseball games, they used to get out in the park, come out there and play baseball. And I mean, it was just that type of a thing. But somewhere down the line, somebody had to take care of business. So Lil was the one that did it. She took care of business and he helped teach him to read and all of that, because he was as blind as a bat.
